result.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
result.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models through forward-only evaluations, but high-dimensional random perturbations can limit optimization efficiency. Sparse perturbations reduce the search dimension, making the selection of informative coordinates critical. We propose Wanda-Importance Sparsity-MeZO (WIS-MeZO), which uses Wanda weight--activation saliency to construct task-conditioned sparse perturbation masks while keeping the pretrained model dense. We analyze support quality through gradient energy capture and relate it to gradient estimation and convergence. Across 16 benchmarks with LLaMA and Qwen models ranging from 3B to 32B parameters, WIS-MeZO achieves higher aggregate scores than MeZO and reaches comparable validation losses in fewer optimization steps. Comparisons with random and magnitude-based sparse perturbations further highlight the importance of informative support selection.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WIS-MeZO，用 Wanda 权重—激活显著性构造任务相关的稀疏扰动掩码，以提升零阶优化的高维搜索效率，并在多个基准与模型规模上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作只关注纯文本 LLM 的零阶微调效率，未涉及多模态表示、latent 推理状态或视觉证据使用；显著性稀疏掩码与 LVR 的贡献分配、证据筛选之间也缺少具体可借鉴的联系。
